A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Algorithms with Calibrated Machine Learning Predictions. All 23 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original evaluations of ski-rental and scheduling algorithms using Citi Bike and sepsis data, with performance results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original algorithm evaluations and their performance results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The calibration-dependent ski-rental rule in Algorithm 1 and the scheduling procedure in Algorithm 3 are unchanged. Predictor and calibration procedures also remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Citi Bike rides for ski rental and sepsis-survival records for scheduling. Appendix C retains the same destination-information scenarios.

E2.justification: Ski rental retains BREAKEVEN, BINARY from Anand et al. (2020), and CONFORMAL from Sun et al. (2024). Scheduling retains the binary-calibration comparison associated with Cho et al. (2022). The newly cited Khodak et al. work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Reported metrics, model configurations, break-even sweeps, and scheduling settings are unchanged, including n = 100 and theta values of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. No new experiment or revised protocol appears.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same feature-information comparisons, base-model comparisons, and parameter-sensitivity results. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The plotted uncertainty displays are identical. V4 adds no run or seed information, statistical explanation of the displays, confidence-level specification, or significance test.

E6.justification: All embedded experimental plots match exactly, and reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Examples include the sepsis predictor's AUC of 0.86 and the comparative findings in Figures 2–3 and 5–9.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, ski-rental guarantees, scheduling lemmas and Theorem 4.3, and proofs in Appendices A and B are unchanged. Equation reflow does not alter their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about calibration, ski-rental guarantees, and scheduling improvements. The related-work addition does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning high variance, predictor granularity, informative features, and the tradeoff between robustness and expected performance are retained. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical feature-selection, model-selection, and calibration details. Code and data access statements are unchanged; relocated footnotes and renamed appendix references provide no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Khodak et al. (2022), Learning predictions for algorithms with predictions, discussing online learning of predictor reliability across repeated problems. It refines the distinction from prior work to statistical uncertainty quantification measures such as calibration, rather than uncertainty quantification generally.

P1.justification: V4 briefly expands and refines Section 1.2, changes main-text references from Appendix A/B/C to Section A/B/C, and updates the version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section order are preserved.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, and Figure 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, with accompanying text and bibliography reflow. The tables and figures retain their content and display designs.

improvement.justification: Section 1.2 now acknowledges research on learning predictor reliability online and states more precisely how calibration differs from that work. This modestly improves the completeness and clarity of research positioning. The methods, theory, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
